protections: P1: target- or response-derived text (fuzzed parameter values, request parts from the input ReqResp, internal-extractor values) must not be evaluated a second time as template expressions against a variable map that holds process environment variables (env is merged by BuildPayloadFromOptions when -ev is set: pkg/protocols/common/generators/options.go:36-38)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the fuzz value map already uses only CLI vars (Options.Vars.AsMap()), not BuildPayloadFromOptions, so env looks excluded
evidence: pkg/fuzz/parts.go:194-196 builds values from Variables, `value` (the target's own parameter value), Options.Vars and input.Values
pkg/fuzz/parts.go:197-199 evaluates the payload, then evaluates the result again, so expression markers inside the substituted target value get resolved
pkg/tmplexec/flow/flow_executor.go:117,120,132 and pkg/tmplexec/multiproto/multi.go:39,42,58 merge BuildPayloadFromOptions (env included) into the template context
pkg/tmplexec/multiproto/multi.go:87-88 and pkg/tmplexec/flow/flow_internal.go:41,78 pass the template context as dynamicValues into the HTTP request
pkg/protocols/http/request.go:517-518 -> pkg/protocols/http/request_fuzz.go:126,147 -> pkg/fuzz/execute.go:156,177 copy it into input.Values

traps.reason_to_dismiss: headless fuzzing is a separate, rarely used protocol, and the report talks about HTTP DAST
evidence: pkg/protocols/headless/request.go:54,61 merge BuildPayloadFromOptions (env) into vars in the plain generic engine, so no flow or multiproto is needed
pkg/protocols/headless/request.go:73,265 pass those vars as fuzz.ExecuteRuleInput.Values, which reach the double evaluation at pkg/fuzz/parts.go:196-199

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the helper exists only to swap in interactsh URLs, runs only when interactsh is configured, and works on 'variables' rather than on the fuzzed value
evidence: pkg/fuzz/execute.go:233-256 calls expressions.Evaluate on every value in input.Values against the same map

input.Values holds target-derived request parts (path, query, body, cookie, header from the ReqResp: pkg/protocols/http/request_fuzz.go:291-318) and internal-extractor values copied from responses into the template context (pkg/tmplexec/multiproto/multi.go:98-115; pkg/tmplexec/flow/flow_internal.go:119-131)
gate: pkg/fuzz/execute.go:224

traps.reason_to_dismiss: getActionArg already rejects unresolved variables with ContainsUnresolvedVariables before evaluating
evidence: pkg/protocols/headless/request.go:247 sets the input to the fuzzed request URL (target-derived)
pkg/protocols/headless/engine/page.go:76-78 merges BuildPayloadFromOptions (env) into payloads again; :88-89 puts the variables built from that URL into the same map

pkg/protocols/headless/engine/page_actions.go:946-948 checks only the template's own argument before substitution; :953 Evaluate substitutes BaseURL etc. and then rescans the substituted text (pkg/protocols/common/expressions/expressions.go:47,53)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the § marker is an internal legacy syntax, so neutralising '{{' in untrusted values looks sufficient
evidence: pkg/protocols/common/replacer/replacer.go:18 replaces {{k}} with values, then :19 runs a second pass with marker.General on the already-substituted output, so a substituted value carrying the General-marker form of an env key is resolved in pass two
pkg/protocols/common/expressions/expressions.go:53 also runs FindExpressions on the post-substitution data

values that must keep working: (a) prefix/postfix/infix rules send the original target value verbatim (pkg/fuzz/parts.go:214-232), even when it contains '{{...}}', e.g. an SSTI probe already in the param; (b) the second evaluation after interactsh replacement (pkg/fuzz/parts.go:198-199) must still resolve template-authored nested expressions; (c) template-authored {{ENV}} references with -ev must still resolve (pkg/protocols/common/generators/options.go:36-38; payload nesting pkg/protocols/http/build_request.go:220-225)
a fix that strips braces from the value, drops the second pass, or removes env globally breaks one of these

traps.reason_to_dismiss: this is ordinary (non-DAST) request chaining that templates rely on, and the report is scoped to DAST/fuzz mode
evidence: pkg/protocols/http/request.go:589 merges extractor DynamicValues (response-derived) into gotDynamicValues; :639-640 feed them into the next Make

pkg/protocols/http/build_request.go:210,217 merges optionVars (env) into allVars; :239 Evaluate substitutes the extracted text and then rescans it (pkg/protocols/common/expressions/expressions.go:47,53), so markers inside a response resolve to env values
the post-dump unresolved-variable check (pkg/protocols/http/request.go:748) passes because the marker is already resolved

masking: If the solver fixes at the source (removes env from fuzz input.Values in pkg/fuzz/execute.go:151-158), T5 stops mattering in the fuzz package. If the solver fixes at the sink by neutralising '{{' in untrusted values, T5 becomes the live bypass. T5's reachability therefore depends on the fix strategy.

conflicts.what: Escaping or stripping '{{' from the target value before parts.go:197 changes the bytes sent in prefix/postfix/infix mode (parts.go:214-232). Dropping the second Evaluate at parts.go:199 breaks nested expressions around interactsh-url.

A shared-layer fix in expressions.evaluate (stop rescanning substituted text at expressions.go:53, or drop the second replacer pass at replacer.go:19) would close T1/T3/T4/T7 at one site, but it risks breaking template-authored nested evaluation, which T6 keeps.
Removing env from headless vars (headless/request.go:54,61; engine/page.go:77) breaks legitimate -ev use in headless templates unless env stays available for template-authored arguments.

fairness_risks: Original target parameter values may legitimately contain '{{...}}' (SSTI probes, client-side template syntax) and must still be sent verbatim in prefix/postfix/infix mode (pkg/fuzz/parts.go:214-232); a rule that refuses or escapes such values contradicts this.
With -ev, template-authored references to env vars (pkg/protocols/common/generators/options.go:36-38) must keep resolving; a test must not require env to be removed outright.
Response chaining via extractors (pkg/protocols/http/request.go:589) must keep substituting the extracted text; only resolving markers inside that text should be refused.
Interactsh-wrapped nested expressions in fuzz payloads rely on the second evaluation (pkg/fuzz/parts.go:198-199).

design.why: T1 (advisory route via the merged template context, M5) anchors the report. T4 (M7 ordering, both types) has a misleading guard before substitution in another package. T7 (M4, deepseek type) gets dismissed as out of DAST scope. T6 (M11, mimo type) penalises over-hardening. T5 (M8, mimo how-type) catches marker-escaping fixes. Each has a different reason to dismiss. T2 and T3 are left out because a single source-side strip in pkg/fuzz/execute.go:151-158 closes them together with T1. The coupled value T6 rules out the one-site shared-layer fix in expressions.evaluate, which keeps T4 and T7 independent of T1.

unverified: Neither the A fix commits (6c803c74d193, d2217320162d) nor the B fix (ccbfb12bd014) could be read, since shell/git was unavailable. The claim that A replaced BuildPayloadFromOptions with Options.Vars.AsMap() in pkg/fuzz (parts.go:196, execute.go:156,177,203) is an inference from the pinned code. The same goes for a_fix_leaves_b_open, b_in_code_a_wrote, and the claim that T1 is B's route.

T4: whether '{{' or the General marker survives retryablehttp Request.String() URL encoding at headless/request.go:247 has not been checked; if it is percent-encoded, T4 may only be reachable through non-encoded parts.
T5: whether a General-marker value in a target parameter survives encoding into the evaluated string has not been checked; T5 may also be judged an encoding variant rather than a trap.
T6: no specific shipped template was found that depends on rescanning substituted text at expressions.go:53; how much legitimate behaviour the shared-layer fix breaks is not verified.
T3 is reachable only when interactsh is configured (pkg/fuzz/execute.go:224); the default interactsh state in DAST runs was not checked.
T7 lies outside the DAST scope of the advisory text; whether the benchmark accepts it as part of the same CWE-200 protection is a policy decision.
independent_groups assumes per-site fixes; a solver who changes expressions.evaluate would close T1, T3, T4 and T7 together if hidden tests do not enforce T6.
